meta.strategy: Stack A — Full Solar-Belly-to-Solar-Cliff Energy Arbitrage (HE10-11 Charge, HE19-20 Discharge)
meta.starting_soc_basis: Conservative assumption: battery depleted from prior day; no confirmed Tenaska carryover data
meta.price_basis: Qualitative structural only — Enverus net load shape + AG2 temperature + Sep 03 reference calibration. No Smartbidder or Yes Energy quantitative forecasts available. Apply ±30% uncertainty band to all price midpoints.
meta.spread_convention: spread = DA minus RT; positive = DA expensive = short DA signal
meta.data_warning: DEGRADED CYCLE — price views are directional estimates only, not model-validated. Yes Energy and Smartbidder both unavailable. Market-analyst guidance: default to energy-only strategy this cycle.

fundamental_inputs.load_peak_note: Broadly flat HE16-18 (80,209 / 80,237 / 80,078 MW). AG2 KDFW 93F (+5F vs Sep 03) suggests actual load may be 81-83 GW.

revenue_summary.scenario_high_assumptions: HE10 at $5, HE11 at $10, HE19 at $140, HE20 at $180, AS at $3/MW-hr

HE01.congestion_note: WEST_TO_NORTH LOW-MEDIUM (P=15-22%); GKS MCC est. -$0.08 to -$0.40/MWh unconditional; no energy position — no congestion impact
HE01.note: High overnight wind 22,504 MW (highest in Sep 2026 series). SOC=0 — cannot offer Non-Spin. Standby.

HE02.note: SOC=0. No NS possible. Wind 21,348 MW (WEST_TO_NORTH MEDIUM SCI ~0.391). Standby.

HE03.note: SOC=0. Wind 20,706 MW (WEST_TO_NORTH MEDIUM SCI ~0.380). Standby.

HE04.note: Wind declining (18,819 MW; SCI ~0.345 borderline). SOC=0. Standby.

HE05.note: Load trough HE05 = 57,732 MW. Wind 17,300 MW. SOC=0. DA est. $18-35 — not worth charging vs HE10-11 ($5-22). Standby.

HE07.note: Morning ramp begins. WDPEAK start HE07. DA est. $30-55/MWh — significantly more expensive than HE10-11. Preserve SOC capacity for optimal charge window. Standby.

HE08.note: Solar onset (689 MW). NL rising. DA est. $30-55/MWh — too expensive vs HE10. Standby.

HE09.note: Solar ramping fast (11,317 MW). NL declining toward trough. DA est. $20-40/MWh — still more expensive than HE10 ($5-22). TRANSITION HOUR: reserve for charge start at HE10. Standby.

HE10.note: PRIMARY CHARGE. Net load series trough 35,398 MW — deepest of Sep 2026 series. Solar 20,551 MW peak-approaching. DA est. $5-22/MWh (midpoint $13.5) — cheapest hour. Full 100 MW DA charge bid at ≤$22/MWh ceiling. Risk: if DA goes NEGATIVE, we get paid to charge (upside). DA-only bid; no RT charge bids.

HE11.soc_calc: 92.2 + 100 MW * 0.922 = 184.4 MWh (physical stored; 92% of 200 MWh nameplate)
HE11.note: SECONDARY CHARGE. NL recovering but solar still very strong (~26 GW est.). DA est. $10-28/MWh (midpoint $19). Full 100 MW. After HE11, physical SOC = 184.4 MWh (total 200 MWh drawn from grid; 170 MWh deliverable at 85% RTE). DA-only charge bid.

HE12.note: Full SOC 184.4 MWh. Solar peak shoulder. DA $25-45 — not worth discharging (HE19-20 spread much better). 25 MW Non-Spin DA: battery has energy, low NS call risk at this hour. Sep 02 precedent confirms NS clearing in shoulder hours.

HE13.note: Solar peak 27,580 MW. Wind floor 5,517 MW. DA $40-65 — still inferior to HE19-20 spread; hold SOC. 25 MW NS.

HE14.note: Wind near floor. DA $40-65. Hold SOC for HE19-20. 25 MW NS.

HE15.note: Solar plateau 27,101 MW. Load 78,500 MW est. DA $40-65 — Sep 04 afternoon much softer than Sep 03 equivalent ($90-130 on Sep 03 due to wind floor near-zero). Wind floor 6,884 MW is healthier. Hold SOC. 25 MW NS.

HE16.note: Load plateau HE16 = 80,209 MW. Solar still substantial (26,500 MW est.). DA $55-90 — would generate positive energy revenue ($72 est.) but opportunity cost vs HE20 ($145 est.) is large. Hold SOC. 25 MW NS.

HE17.note: Load peak HE17 = 80,237 MW. Solar declining. DA $55-90 — opportunity cost vs HE20 is still large ($72 vs $145 est.). Hold SOC. 25 MW NS. SOC CONFIRMATION CHECKPOINT: verify physical SOC >= 180 MWh before submitting HE19-20 DA discharge bids.

HE18.note: Solar declining (est. ~20 GW). DA $65-100 — approaching range where partial discharge would be viable, but opportunity cost vs HE19-20 still justifies holding full SOC. MANDATORY GATE: confirm physical SOC >= 180 MWh before proceeding. If SOC < 180 MWh, cancel HE19-20 DA discharge commitments immediately to prevent RT imbalance cascade (ref Aug 31 precedent: -$25,691 RT loss).

HE19.da_rt_direction: UNCERTAIN — RT may spike above DA as solar cliff onset generates real-time scarcity faster than DAM anticipates
HE19.rt_headroom_note: 30 MW held from DA: (1) required by RTE physics to preserve 108.5 MWh for HE20 100 MW dispatch; (2) RT optionality hedge if RT > DA at HE19
HE19.note: DISCHARGE HOUR 1 (RTE-constrained). Solar cliff onset: solar 13,193 MW dropping to 2,395 MW NEXT hour. NL 51,566 MW surging. DA est. $90-140/MWh (midpoint $115). 70 MW DA (not 100 MW) — required to preserve SOC for HE20 full 100 MW dispatch. Energy revenue: 70 MWh * $115 = $8,050. AS zeroed: no overlap with energy dispatch hours.

HE20.da_rt_direction: DA_PRIMARY — wind buffer 16,358 MW reduces RT spike probability; DA certainty at $110-180 preferred over RT optionality
HE20.p_rt_above_300_note: Reduced from Sep 03 6-12% due to +2,370 MW wind advantage
HE20.note: PRIMARY DISCHARGE HOUR. Net load peak 57,400 MW — solar effectively zero (2,395 MW), wind 16,358 MW (buffer). DA est. $110-180/MWh (midpoint $145). Full 100 MW DA dispatch. Battery depleted at end of HE20 (SOC 108.5 -> 0.0 MWh). RTE check: 170 MWh total delivered (70 HE19 + 100 HE20) from 200 MWh drawn (100 HE10 + 100 HE11) = 85% RTE verified.

HE21.note: SOC depleted (0 MWh). Cannot discharge or offer AS products requiring energy. Wind recovering 17,172 MW. NL elevated 56,674 MW. Standby. Reference: Sep 02 HE21 RT spike $106.63 captured fortuitously — no analogous opportunity can be pre-planned with SOC=0.

HE22.congestion_note: WEST_TO_NORTH late-night surge MEDIUM P(binding)=12-20%; GKS MCC -$0.4 to -$1.5/MWh if binding; SOC=0 so no impact
HE22.note: SOC depleted. No energy or AS possible. Wind surge building 19,663 MW (WEST_TO_NORTH late-night onset; SCI ~0.361). Standby.

HE23.note: SOC depleted. Wind 20,842 MW (WEST_TO_NORTH MEDIUM SCI ~0.382). DA $20-38/MWh — too expensive for D+2 positioning recharge vs opportunity cost. Standby.

HE24.note: SOC depleted. Wind 21,398 MW (WEST_TO_NORTH late-night MEDIUM; SCI ~0.392). DA $20-38 — recharge at this price reduces D+5 Sep 04 net revenue without confirmed D+2 price advantage. Standby. D+2 (Sep 05) recharge decision deferred to Sep 04 daily cycle.

soc_profile.max_soc_hours: HE11 through HE18 (7 hours at full stored capacity)

as_venue_summary.ns_soc_risk_note: 25 MW NS × 30 min × 1/0.922 = max 13.6 MWh SOC draw per call event. From 184.4 MWh, residual = 170.8 MWh — still sufficient for HE19-20 discharge plan. Set NS offer price >= $3/MW-hr to limit call frequency.

alternative_stacks.stack_b_he20_modification: Reduce HE20 DA from 100 MW to 70 MW — reserve 30 MW for RT at peak hour

alternative_stacks.stack_b_downside: -$1,500 to -$3,000 if RT stays below DA at HE19-20

self_review_reference.root_cause_2: HE19 RT imbalance: -$2,227 from DA discharge committed on under-charged battery
self_review_reference.root_cause_3: NonSpin cleared at 57 MW avg vs 80-100 MW planned
self_review_reference.sep04_improvement_1: DA charge bid ceiling set ≤$22/MWh (vs ≤$35 on Sep 02) — more competitive
self_review_reference.sep04_improvement_2: SOC confirmation gate at HE18: cancel HE19-20 DA discharge if SOC < 180 MWh
self_review_reference.sep04_improvement_3: AS reduced to 25 MW NS hold phase only (vs 80-100 MW) — eliminates over-commitment cascade risk
self_review_reference.sep04_improvement_4: HE19 discharge 70 MW (not 100 MW) — RTE-correct scheduling eliminates over-dispatch RT imbalance
